content.text: Definitive answer: **no.** The subagent transcript lands on the shadow branch only, and after the commit it exists nowhere — the shadow branch is deleted at condensation and the committed checkpoint never had it. My PR description overstated it. Fixing that now:

input.command:
gh pr edit 1935 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` resolved the subagent transcript as a **sibling** of the main transcript:

```
<transcriptDir>/agent-<agentID>.jsonl
```

Claude Code (verified on 2.1.221) nests them one level deeper:

```
<transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<agentID>.jsonl
<transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<agentID>.meta.json   # agentType, description, toolUseId, spawnDepth
```

So the resolved path never existed and `SubagentTranscriptPath` was always empty in production. Evidence: across three enabled repos, **every** real `"subagent completed"` log line carries `agent_id` but never the `subagent_transcript` attribute — that attribute is only appended when the path resolves.

Two consequences:

1. The shadow-branch task checkpoint stored **no subagent transcript** — `.entire/metadata/<session>/tasks/<tool-use-id>/` held only `checkpoint.json`.
2. File extraction fell back to scanning the **main** transcript from offset 0, where a subagent's `Write`/`Edit` calls never appear.

The turn-end extractor already used the correct nested path, so a subagent's files were still picked up at Stop. That masked the bug.

## Scope — what this does and does not fix

This restores the capture at `SubagentEnd`, which is **shadow-branch (ephemeral) only**. Verified end to end on this branch:

```
# shadow branch, after post-task
.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl
.entire/metadata/<session>/tasks/toolu_.../agent-<id>.jsonl   <-- restored by this PR
.entire/metadata/<session>/tasks/toolu_.../checkpoint.json

# committed checkpoint, after the user commits
0/content_hash.txt  0/full.jsonl  0/metadata.json  0/prompt.txt  0/transcript.jsonl  metadata.json
```

`extractSessionData` reads only `full.jsonl` + `prompt.txt` out of the shadow tree, so `tasks/` is dropped at condensation and the shadow branch is then deleted — after the commit the subagent transcript is reachable from no ref at all. (Consistent with the wider survey: 0 of 80 primary checkpoint refs in this repo contain a `tasks/` path.)

So what this PR buys today:

- Correct `ModifiedFiles` on the task step — extracted from the subagent's own transcript instead of the main one.
- In-session task checkpoints (`entire checkpoint list`, rewind) actually carry the subagent transcript until the next commit.
- A working resolver, which is a prerequisite for carrying subagent data into committed checkpoints.

Making subagent detail survive a commit is separate follow-up work: it needs condensation to carry `tasks/` into the committed tree (the persistent store already has the layout and an `IsTask` flag, but no production path writes it), and a decision on what the committed record should contain. Not in this PR.

## Fix

- `ResolveAgentTranscriptPath(transcriptDir, sessionID, agentID)` — prefers the nested layout, falls back to the legacy sibling layout so sessions from older agent versions keep working, returns `""` when neither exists (and never resolves an empty `agentID`).
- `SubagentsDir(transcriptDir, sessionID)` — one definition of the nested directory; the turn-end extractor now uses it too instead of inlining the join.

The `meta.json` sidecar is documented but not yet consumed — richer subagent attribution is part of the follow-up above.

## Tests

- `TestResolveAgentTranscriptPath` — nested, legacy, nested-wins-over-legacy, neither-exists, empty-agent-ID.
- `TestSubagentCheckpoints_StoresSubagentTranscript_CurrentLayout` (integration) — asserts the shadow branch contains `tasks/<tool-use-id>/agent-<id>.jsonl` and that it references the subagent's edit. **Verified RED before the fix**, green after.
- `TestSubagentCheckpoints_StoresSubagentTranscript_LegacyLayout` (integration) — regression guard for the old layout.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" && echo "PR body updated"

The CLI only checked the legacy sibling path, so SubagentTranscriptPath was always empty in production — confirmed across three enabled repos, where no real "subagent completed" log line ever carries the subagent_transcript attribute. Consequences: the shadow-branch task checkpoint stored no subagent transcript, and file extraction fell back to scanning the main transcript, where a subagent's Write/Edit calls never appear. The turn-end extractor already used the correct nested path, so files were still picked up at Stop — which masked the bug.

Solution:
Add ResolveAgentTranscriptPath(), which prefers the current nested layout and falls back to the legacy sibling path for older sessions (and never resolves an empty agentID). Add SubagentsDir() as the single definition of the nested directory and route the turn-end extractor through it too. Update handleLifecycleSubagentEnd() to use the resolver. Unit tests cover all layout permutations; two integration tests assert the shadow branch actually contains tasks/<tool-use-id>/agent-<id>.jsonl for the current and legacy layouts (the current-layout one verified RED before the fix).

Condensation's extractSessionData reads just full.jsonl + prompt.txt out of the shadow tree, so tasks/ is dropped, and the shadow branch is deleted afterwards — after the user commits, the subagent transcript is reachable from no ref at all. (Survey: 0 of 80 primary checkpoint refs in this repo contain a tasks/ path.)

What this change buys today: correct ModifiedFiles on the task step, since they now come from the subagent's own transcript; in-session task checkpoints that actually carry the subagent transcript until the next commit; and a working resolver as a prerequisite for carrying subagent data into committed checkpoints.

Making subagent detail survive a commit is separate follow-up work: condensation must carry tasks/ into the committed tree (the persistent store already has the layout and an IsTask flag, but no production path writes them), and the committed record needs enriching — today's task checkpoint.json holds only session_id, tool_use_id, checkpoint_uuid and agent_id, with no subagent type, description, files or tokens. Not in this change.
EOF

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

## Findings

### 1. Newly activated read + full redaction of the subagent transcript on every SubagentStop (intended cost, but measure it)
- **File/line:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1149` (consumed at `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:550` and `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/ephemeral.go:444`)
- **Concrete waste:** Before the fix, `subagentTranscriptPath` was `""` for every modern Claude Code session, so the store's `os.ReadFile` + `redact.JSONLBytes` branch was dead code. It is now live on every subagent completion. I benchmarked the repo's own redaction bench: `BenchmarkRedactJSONLBytes/Fixture/ClaudeFull2` runs at **4.07 MB/s, 287 ms for a 1.17 MB transcript** (M4 Max, 48 MB allocated, 447k allocs). `redact.JSONLBytes` also makes two full copies of the content (`string(b)` in, `[]byte(redacted)` out). Unlike the main transcript, the subagent blob has **no chunking and no size cap**. Additionally the same file is now read and JSON-parsed **twice** in one hook process: once by `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` (lifecycle.go:1171) and again by the store's `os.ReadFile`.
- **Honest net:** this partly *pays for itself* — extraction now scans the small subagent transcript instead of the whole main transcript from offset 0. I measured full-transcript parse at **231 MB/s** (5 ms/MB), so the extraction saving is ~5 ms/MB of main transcript while the redaction add is ~250 ms/MB of subagent transcript. Net is a modest regression dominated by redaction throughput.
- **Cheaper alternative:** none that preserves the fix's intent — you cannot store the transcript without redacting it. Worth doing anyway: (a) add a size guard so a pathological multi-MB subagent transcript can't add seconds to the hook (mirroring the main transcript's cap), and (b) if you want the duplicate read/parse gone, thread the already-read bytes through `TaskStepContext` instead of a path. 67	func WorktreeRoot(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
68		// Get current working directory to check cache validity
69		cwd, err := os.Getwd() //nolint:forbidigo // already present in codebase
70		if err != nil {
71			cwd = ""
72		}
73	
74		// Check cache with read lock first
75		worktreeRootMu.RLock()
76		if worktreeRootCache != "" && worktreeRootCacheDir == cwd {
77			cached := worktreeRootCache
78			worktreeRootMu.RUnlock()
79			return cached, nil
80		}
81		worktreeRootMu.RUnlock()
82	
83		// Cache miss - get worktree root and update cache with write lock
84		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
85		output, err := cmd.Output()
86		if err != nil {
87			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get git worktree root: %w", err)
88		}
89	
90		root := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
91	
92		worktreeRootMu.Lock()
93		worktreeRootCache = root
94		worktreeRootCacheDir = cwd
95		worktreeRootMu.Unlock()
96	
97		return root, nil
98	}

102	func ClearWorktreeRootCache() {

105		worktreeRootCacheDir = ""

126	// (i.e., inside the .entire directory). It is used only to EXCLUDE infra paths
127	// from checkpoints/tracking, so it matches case-insensitively on
128	// case-insensitive filesystems via IsProtectedSubpath. Do not use it as a
129	// containment/allow gate.
130	func IsInfrastructurePath(path string) bool {
131		return IsProtectedSubpath(EntireDir, path)
132	}

134	// IsSubpath reports whether child is lexically under parent (or equal to it).
135	// It uses filepath.Rel, which cleans both inputs and is traversal-resistant:
136	// a crafted child like "/a/b/../../../etc/passwd" that escapes parent will
137	// produce a relative path starting with ".." and be rejected.
138	//
139	// Matching is case-SENSITIVE. This is the correct primitive for fail-closed
140	// containment/allow checks (e.g. validating an attacker-influenced path stays
141	// under an Entire-owned dir): on a case-sensitive volume a differently-cased
142	// path names a different directory, so folding it in would fail open. For
143	// EXCLUSION decisions that must also catch case variants on Windows/macOS, use
144	// IsProtectedSubpath instead.
145	func IsSubpath(parent, child string) bool {
146		rel, err := filepath.Rel(parent, child)
147		if err != nil {
148			return false
149		}
150		return !IsRelativeTraversal(rel)
151	}

153	// IsProtectedSubpath reports whether child is under parent for the purpose of
154	// EXCLUDING protected/infrastructure content from checkpoints and tracking.
155	// Unlike IsSubpath it honors OS case-insensitivity (see CaseInsensitiveFS), so
156	// a case variant of a protected dir (".Claude" vs ".claude") is still excluded
157	// on Windows/macOS.
158	//
159	// SECURITY: never use this for allow/containment decisions. Case-folding widens
160	// what counts as "inside" parent, which is safe only when the effect is to
161	// exclude more. On a case-sensitive volume under a case-insensitive GOOS it
162	// over-matches; for a fail-closed gate that would fail open. Use IsSubpath there.
163	func IsProtectedSubpath(parent, child string) bool {
164		if CaseInsensitiveFS() {
165			return IsSubpath(strings.ToLower(parent), strings.ToLower(child))
166		}
167		return IsSubpath(parent, child)
168	}

171	// on the host OS. This is OS-based, not volume-based: Windows and macOS default
172	// to case-insensitive filesystems, Linux to case-sensitive. Keying on GOOS keeps
173	// the result deterministic. It must only influence EXCLUSION decisions (see
174	// IsProtectedSubpath / Equal): on an atypical volume (e.g. a case-sensitive
175	// macOS APFS volume) it treats a differently-cased path as matching, which is
176	// safe only when the effect is to exclude more, never to widen an allow gate.
177	func CaseInsensitiveFS() bool {
178		return runtime.GOOS == osWindows || runtime.GOOS == osDarwin
179	}
180	
181	// Equal reports whether two paths refer to the same location, honoring the host
182	// OS's case sensitivity (see CaseInsensitiveFS). Both inputs are cleaned and
183	// slash-normalized before comparison. Like IsProtectedSubpath, this is intended
184	// for EXCLUSION matching (e.g. protected files), not fail-closed containment.
185	func Equal(a, b string) bool {
186		a = filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(a))
187		b = filepath.Clean(filepath.FromSlash(b))
188		if CaseInsensitiveFS() {
189			return strings.EqualFold(a, b)
190		}
191		return a == b
192	}

196	func IsRelativeTraversal(rel string) bool {
197		return rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, "../") || strings.HasPrefix(rel, `..\`)
198	}

1	# Entire CLI Hooks for Claude Code
2	
3	This document describes the hooks that Entire installs in Claude Code's `.claude/settings.json` to track AI-assisted development sessions.
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	Entire integrates with Claude Code through six hooks that fire at different points during a session:
8	
9	| Hook                     | Trigger                        | Purpose                                        |
10	| ------------------------ | ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
11	| `SessionStart`           | New chat session begins        | Generate and persist Entire session ID         |
12	| `UserPromptSubmit`       | User submits a prompt          | Capture pre-prompt state, check for conflicts  |
13	| `Stop`                   | Claude finishes responding     | Create checkpoint with code + metadata         |
14	| `PreToolUse[Agent]`      | Subagent is about to start     | Capture pre-task state for diff computation    |
15	| `PostToolUse[Agent]`     | Subagent finishes              | Create final checkpoint for subagent work      |
16	| `PostToolUse[TaskCreate\|TaskUpdate]` | Subagent updates its task list | Create incremental checkpoint if files changed |
17	
18	> **Tool matcher note.** Claude Code's subagent dispatch tool is `Agent` (there
19	> was never a `Task` tool), and the `TodoWrite` tool was disabled by default in
20	> v2.1.142 in favor of `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`. Older CLI versions installed
21	> these hooks under `Task`/`TodoWrite`, where they silently never fired. A normal
22	> `entire enable` does not rewrite existing hook config in place; re-run with
23	> `--force` (`entire enable --force`) to strip the stale entries and reinstall
24	> under the matchers above. See
25	> [tools-reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference.md) and
26	> [hooks matcher rules](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md).
27	>
28	> The incremental-checkpoint handler still parses the legacy `TodoWrite`
29	> `tool_input` schema for its checkpoint message label; under `TaskCreate`/
30	> `TaskUpdate` the checkpoint is still created (file-change detection is
31	> independent) but the label falls back to `Checkpoint #N`. Richer labels from
32	> the Task* payloads are a follow-up.
33	
34	### Critical Capabilities
35	
36	  1. Prompt blocking - UserPromptSubmit hook needs to support returning a response to be shown in the cli session.
37	    - Claude Code allows us to return a JSON response to stdout that can:
38	      - Allow continuation: {"continue": true}
39	      - Block with message: {"continue": false, "stopReason": "Your message here"}
40	  2. Transcript access - Hooks receive transcript path; system needs to read it for:
41	    - Extracting user prompts
42	    - Extracting modified files
43	    - Generating summaries
44	  3. Tool use ID tracking - For subagent checkpoints, need unique tool_use_id to correlate PreToolUse and PostToolUse events
45	  4. Stdin parsing - Hook input comes as JSON on stdin; agent must define its input schema
46	
47	## Detailed Hook Info
48	
49	### `SessionStart`
50	
51	- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code session-start`
52	- **Handler**: `handleSessionStart()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:907`
53	
54	Fires when a new chat session begins in Claude Code.
55	
56	**What it does:**
57	
58	1.  **Parse Input**: Reads session details from Claude Code's hook payload (`session_id`, `session_ref`).
59	2.  **Generate Entire Session ID**: Creates a date-prefixed identifier by combining today's date with the model's session ID (e.g., `2026-01-15-ab310c99-f579-4a12-8b3c-1234567890ab`).
60	3.  **Persist Session ID**: Writes the Entire session ID to `.entire/current_session`. This file is read by subsequent hooks to maintain session context across hook invocations, even if the session spans midnight (date boundary).
61	
62	### `UserPromptSubmit`
63	
64	- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit`
65	- **Handler**: `captureInitialState()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:248`
66	
67	Fires every time the user submits a prompt. Prepares the repository state tracking _before_ Claude makes any changes.
68	
69	**What it does:**
70	
71	1.  **Concurrent Session Check**:
72	
73	    - Queries the strategy to check if another Entire session has uncommitted checkpoints on the same HEAD commit.
74	    - If a conflict is found, outputs a JSON response that blocks the prompt and shows a warning to the user.
75	    - The warning includes the other session's initial prompt (if available) and a resume command.
76	    - Sets `ConcurrentWarningShown` flag in session state so the user can continue on the next prompt.
77	    - Once the user commits their changes (or the conflict resolves), the flag is cleared automatically.
78	
79	2.  **Capture Pre-Prompt State**:
80	
81	    - Runs `git status` to get a list of all **untracked files** in the repository.
82	    - Saves this list to `.entire/tmp/pre-prompt-<session-id>.json`.
83	    - This baseline is compared later (in the `Stop` hook) to determine which files were newly created by Claude.
84	    - Records the current transcript line count (`StepTranscriptStart`) for incremental token usage calculation.
85	
86	3.  **Initialize Session Strategy**:
87	    - For strategies that implement `SessionInitializer`, calls `InitializeSession()`.
88	    - **Manual-commit strategy**: Creates or validates the shadow branch (`entire/<HEAD-hash[:7]>`), saves session state to `.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json` with `BaseCommit`, `WorktreePath`, and `AgentType`.
89	    - Handles shadow branch conflicts (from other worktrees) and session ID conflicts with appropriate error messages and recovery options.
90	
91	### `Stop`
92	
93	- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code stop`
94	- **Handler**: `commitWithMetadata()` in `hooks_claudecode_handlers.go:288`
95	
96	Fires when Claude finishes responding. Does **not** fire on user interrupt (Ctrl+C).
97	
98	**What it does:**
99	
100	1.  **Parse Transcript**:
101	
102	    - Reads the JSONL transcript from the path provided by Claude Code.
103	    - Parses the full transcript. `CheckpointTranscriptStart` (or `StepTranscriptStart` from pre-prompt state) is used to detect whether new content exists since the last checkpoint.
104	    - Extracts **modified files** by scanning for Write/Edit tool uses in the transcript.
105	
106	2.  **Extract and Save Metadata** (to `.entire/metadata/<session-id>/`):
107	
108	    - `full.jsonl` - Copy of the complete transcript.
109	    - `prompt.txt` - Checkpoint-scoped user prompts, separated by `---`.
110	    - `summary.txt` - The last assistant message (used as checkpoint summary).
111	
112	3.  **Compute File Changes**:
113	
114	    - **Modified files**: Extracted from transcript (Write/Edit tool invocations).
115	    - **New files**: Compare current untracked files against pre-prompt state to find files created by Claude.
116	    - **Deleted files**: Query `git status` for tracked files that no longer exist.
117	    - All paths are normalized relative to repo root (not cwd) to handle Claude running from subdirectories.
118	
119	4.  **Generate Commit Message**: Derives from the last user prompt, truncated and formatted appropriately.
120	
121	5.  **Calculate Token Usage**:
122	
123	    - Parses the transcript from `StepTranscriptStart` (captured at prompt start) to calculate tokens used in this turn.
124	    - Extracts token counts from assistant messages: input tokens, cache creation/read tokens, output tokens.
125	    - Deduplicates by message ID (streaming creates multiple rows per message; uses highest output_tokens).
126	    - Finds spawned subagents by scanning for `agentId:` in Task tool results.
127	    - Calculates subagent token usage from their transcript files (`agent-<id>.jsonl`).
128	    - Aggregates into a `TokenUsage` struct with nested `SubagentTokens`.
129	
130	6.  **Invoke Strategy**:
131	
132	    - Builds a `SaveContext` with session ID, file lists, metadata paths, git author info, and token usage.
133	    - Calls `strategy.SaveChanges(ctx)` to create the checkpoint.

Background: Pi has no subagent events. Subagent extensions spawn a nested `pi --mode json -p --no-session` process from the project dir, which auto-discovers Entire's project-local extension and fires Entire's hooks as if it were the user's session. Your ONLY angle is REUSE: flag new code that re-implements something the codebase already has.

Specific things worth checking:

Grep for existing sentinels and guards: shouldReportForwardedHook / shouldSkipForwardedHook in cmd/entire/cli/hook_registry.go, the agent sentinels in cmd/entire/cli/interactive (GEMINI_CLI, COPILOT_CLI, PI_CODING_AGENT), cmd/entire/cli/agent/spawn, and anything in cmd/entire/cli/agent/*/lifecycle.go that returns nil to skip an event. Is there an existing convention or helper for "this hook invocation is not ours, skip it" that this should use instead of a pi-local function?
- Is there an existing env-var naming convention for Entire-set process markers (grep ENTIRE_ prefixed env vars, especially ones set by Entire for child processes, e.g. in cmd/entire/cli/agent/spawn and execx)? Does ENTIRE_PI_NESTED fit it? Is there a central place where ENTIRE_* env var names are declared as constants rather than inline string literals?
- logNestedInvocationSkip is a new 3-line logging wrapper. Is there an existing skip-logging helper or convention in the agent packages?

Do NOT report correctness bugs. Report only reuse findings, each with file, line, one-line summary, the concrete duplication cost, and the exact existing helper/convention to use instead. Verify every claim by reading the code. If you find nothing, say so explicitly.

You are doing an ALTITUDE review of a diff in the repo at /Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2 (currently on branch soph/fix-pi-nested-subagent-session).

Get the diff with: git diff main...HEAD

Scope: cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/lifecycle.go, cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/entire_extension.ts, cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/nested_session_test.go, cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/hooks_test.go

Your ONLY angle is ALTITUDE: is the fix at the right depth, or a fragile bandaid? Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough.

Background: Pi has no subagent lifecycle events. A Pi subagent extension spawns a nested `pi --mode json -p --no-session` process with cwd inside the project; Pi auto-discovers the project-local Entire extension there, so the child fires Entire's hooks as though it were the user's own session. With --no-session it reports no session file, and the per-repo session-ID cache is a single file, so the child was handed its parent's session ID and corrupted the parent's prompt and turn window.

The fix has two layers: an ENTIRE_PI_NESTED env marker set/checked in the TypeScript extension, and a Go-side `nestedInvocation()` guard that refuses to resolve a cache fallback when the payload has no session file.

Key altitude questions to investigate and answer definitively:
1. Is "nested agent process fires our hooks" a Pi-specific problem or a general one? Investigate whether other agents can be nested the same way (e.g. an agent's bash tool running `claude -p`, `codex exec`, or `pi -p`; MCP hosts; `entire review`/`entire investigate` spawning an agent — see cmd/entire/cli/agent/spawn and the review/investigate session adoption via ENTIRE_REVIEW_SESSION / ENTIRE_INVESTIGATE_SESSION env vars in cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go). If it is general, should the guard live in the shared dispatcher (cmd/entire/cli/hook_registry.go executeAgentHook, or DispatchLifecycleEvent) rather than in one agent's ParseHookEvent? Note that cmd/entire/cli/hook_registry.go already has shouldSkipForwardedHook for a related "this hook isn't ours" case (cross-agent forwarding from Cursor) — compare the two and say whether they should be one mechanism.
2. The env marker is set by the extension in the pi process, and Entire's own hook subprocesses inherit it. The diff documents that the CLI must NOT read it. Is that split a sound design, or is it a trap that will be tripped later? Is there a more robust signal available (e.g. the extension passing an explicit "nested" field in the hook payload JSON, or passing the parent session ID, or the Go side comparing a process/session identity)? Assess whether declaring nestedness IN THE PAYLOAD would be strictly better than an inherited env var, given the extension already controls the payload shape.
3. The Go guard infers nestedness from an absence (no session file). Is inferring from absence the right depth, or should the sessionless case be handled as its own explicit concept (an ephemeral/untracked session) rather than conflated with "nested"? Note the guard also silently disables tracking for a legitimate user-run `pi --no-session` session, and judge whether conflating those two cases is acceptable.

Be concrete and decisive. If the answer is "correct for this fix, follow-up for the general mechanism", say so plainly. Do NOT report correctness bugs. Report findings with file, line, one-line summary, concrete maintenance cost, and the deeper alternative.

content.text:
#1935's simplify pass is pushed. Here's what it changed, and #1936's review is now running.

**#1935 — the reviews found a real problem with my fix, not just polish.** All four independently converged on it: I'd put the new `SubagentsDir` helper in package `cli`, which is the one package the other copies *cannot* import (`cli` imports `strategy`/`review`/`agentimport`). So the "single source of truth" I added was actually the 5th copy, on the wrong side of the import graph.

Full inventory: **10 duplicated literals** — 5 of the `<dir>/<sessionID>/subagents` join and 5 of the `agent-<id>.jsonl` join, spread across `cli`, `review`, `agentimport`, `strategy`, `claudecode`, `factoryaidroid`. That half-encoded layout is precisely how the original bug hid: turn-end already assumed the nested layout while SubagentEnd assumed the flat sibling, and nothing forced them to agree.

Moved both to `paths` (verified leaf package, no internal deps, already imported by every site including the agent packages) and converted all ten sites. Also applied:

- Folded the legacy path builder into the resolver as two early returns — it had no callers left, so exporting it kept the wrong-by-default builder as discoverable as the safe one.
- Replaced my hand-rolled shadow-branch reader with the existing `env.ReadFileFromBranch`. Mine duplicated 38 lines, **opened the repo with `git.PlainOpen` — which CLAUDE.md forbids outside `gitrepo`** — never closed the handle, and walked the whole tree fetching a blob per file.
- Collapsed the two near-copy tests into one table test; the legacy copy had already drifted and lost its content assertion.
- Moved the subagent-transcript writers into the harness so they stop being a per-test copy of the layout.
- Dropped the `.meta.json` fixture (nothing reads it), deleted two tests whose coverage the resolver test already provides, and de-triplicated the rationale.

Re-verified RED against `main` with the refactored test — nested row fails, legacy row passes, matching pre-fix behaviour. `mise run check` green.

**Two findings I deliberately did not apply**, both worth their own PR rather than being smuggled into a bug fix:

1. **New unbounded cost on the hook path.** The subagent transcript read + redaction was dead code before (the path never resolved); it's now live on every subagent completion. The efficiency review benchmarked this repo's own redaction at **~250ms per MB**, and unlike the main transcript this blob has *no chunking and no size cap*. It partly pays for itself (extraction now scans the small subagent transcript instead of the whole main one at ~5ms/MB), but a cap is a behavior decision.
2. **A pre-existing ~5ms/MB waste per turn end**: `ExtractAllModifiedFiles`'s documented `subagentsDir == ""` short-circuit is unreachable from both callers, so every turn end parses the full main transcript twice — ~90ms on a 20MB session. Now a 2-line fix thanks to the `paths` move.

<result>## Bottom line

`nestedInvocation()` in `pi/lifecycle.go` does **not** duplicate any existing helper. There is **no shared abstraction** for "this is a nested/subagent invocation, don't treat it as the user's session." What exists is two independent, per-agent, payload-shape-specific guards (pi and copilot-cli) plus a separate cross-agent *hook-forwarding* guard that solves a different problem (wrong agent, not wrong nesting level).

---

## 1. Every `nil, nil` skip in `ParseHookEvent` paths, characterized

Only **two** agents skip because the event came from a subagent / nested / sessionless process: **pi** and **copilotcli**. Everything else is "hook has no lifecycle meaning" or "payload lacks required data."

### The two nesting/subagent guards

**copilotcli — subagent detected by session-ID shape** (`/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/agent/copilotcli/lifecycle.go`)
- `:17` — `const subagentSessionIDPrefix = "toolu_"`
- `:21` — `func isSubagentSessionID(sessionID string) bool` → `strings.HasPrefix(sessionID, subagentSessionIDPrefix)`
- `:92-96` — the guard:
```go
if hookName != HookNameSubagentStop && isSubagentSessionID(env.SessionID) {
    logging.Debug(ctx, "copilot-cli: skipping lifecycle event for subagent session", ...)
    return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // Subagent lifecycle hook — no top-level session action.
}
```
WHY (comment `:84-91`): Copilot fires per-turn/session hooks for subagent turns using the Task tool-use id as sessionId; a phantom session would never get a matching stop and would pin its shadow branch open forever. Note it is a *blanket* pre-switch guard with a single carve-out for `subagent-stop`.

**pi — nested detected by absence of a session file** (`/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/lifecycle.go`)
- `:166` — `func nestedInvocation(payload piHookPayload, sessionID string) bool` → `return sessionID == "" && payload.SessionFile == ""`
- `:170` — `func logNestedInvocationSkip(ctx context.Context, hookName string)`
- `:195-199` — `session_start`: `if sessionID == ""` → skip (does **not** call `nestedInvocation`; it's the stricter subset)
- `:209-212` — `before_agent_start`: `if nestedInvocation(payload, sessionID)` → skip
- `:233-236` — `agent_end`: `if nestedInvocation(payload, sessionID)` → skip

WHY (comment `:145-165`): Pi has no subagent events; subagents are a nested `pi --mode json -p --no-session` child that auto-loads Entire's project-local extension and fires the same hooks. With `--no-session` there's no session file, so the per-repo session-ID cache handed the child its *parent's* session ID, overwriting the parent's prompt and opening a turn mid-flight.

### All other `nil, nil` skips (none are nesting-related)

| file:line | condition | reason |
|---|---|---|
| `claudecode/lifecycle.go:88` | `case HookNamePostTodo` | Claude-specific, handled outside the dispatcher (see `hook_registry.go:172,211`) |
| `claudecode/lifecycle.go:90` | `default` | unknown hook |
| `codex/lifecycle.go:80` | `case HookNamePreToolUse` | pass-through |
| `codex/lifecycle.go:84` | `default` | unknown hook |
| `codex/lifecycle.go:137` | `if !isApplyPatchTool(raw.ToolName)` | non-mutating tool (shell/MCP) |
| `codex/lifecycle.go:147` | no added/modified/deleted paths | empty/unparseable apply_patch envelope |
| `copilotcli/lifecycle.go:65` | `PreToolUse, PostToolUse, ErrorOccurred` | pass-through, skips reading stdin |
| `copilotcli/lifecycle.go:80` | `env.Host == HostVSCode && !validateVSCodeEvent(env, hookName)` | VS Code `hookEventName` ≠ CLI subcommand |
| `copilotcli/lifecycle.go:111` | `default` | unknown hook |
| `cursor/lifecycle.go:45` | `default` | unknown hook |
| `cursor/lifecycle.go:191` | `if raw.Task == ""` in `parseSubagentStart` | missing task text — data gap, **not** a nesting skip |
| `cursor/lifecycle.go:211` | `if raw.Task == ""` in `parseSubagentStop` | same |
| `factoryaidroid/lifecycle.go:73` | `case HookNameSubagentStop, HookNameNotification` | "acknowledged hooks with no lifecycle action" — droid maps Pre/PostToolUse to Subagent{Start,End} instead, so its native `subagent-stop` is intentionally inert |
| `factoryaidroid/lifecycle.go:75` | `default` | unknown hook |
| `geminicli/lifecycle.go:95` | `BeforeTool, AfterTool, AfterModel, BeforeToolSelection, Notification` | acknowledged, no lifecycle action |
| `geminicli/lifecycle.go:97` | `default` | unknown hook |
| `geminicli/lifecycle.go:197` | `if model == ""` in `parseBeforeModel` | no model info |
| `opencode/lifecycle.go:34` | `strings.TrimSpace(inj.Text) == ""` | this is `RenderContextInjection`, not ParseHookEvent |
| `opencode/lifecycle.go:138` | `default` | unknown hook. OpenCode has **no** subagent hooks at all |
| `pi/lifecycle.go:69` | empty injection text | `RenderContextInjection`, not ParseHookEvent |
| `pi/lifecycle.go:271` | `case HookNameSessionShutdown` | cleanup-only (clears session cache); deliberately no `SessionEnd` to avoid racing `agent_end` |
| `pi/lifecycle.go:275` | `default` | unknown hook |
| `vogon/hooks.go:63` | `default` | unknown hook. Vogon has no subagent hooks |
| `external/external.go:250` | stdout == `null` | protocol contract: subprocess said "no event" |

Verified — and it means something I published is wrong.

`extractSessionIDFromPath("/tmp/live.jsonl")` returns `"live"`: the function falls back to the basename, so a session file that's present but unparseable **always** yields a non-empty session ID. Therefore:

- The `payload.SessionFile == ""` term in my `nestedInvocation` predicate is inert — `sessionID == ""` already implies it.
- My stated justification for that term, in the #1936 PR body and trail 998 — *"the legitimate cache fallback: session file present, but its name carries no parseable ID"* — describes a case that **never reaches the cache**. The claim is wrong, and it was the sole rationale offered for the redundant term.

The guard's real effect is simpler than I described: no resolvable session ID → skip. I'll correct the PR body and trail along with the code once the remaining three reviews land — the altitude review is weighing whether nestedness should be declared in the hook payload instead of via an inherited env var, which could reshape this further, so I don't want to edit twice.

## Verdict

The fix is at an acceptable layer and ships safely, but it is a bandaid in one precise sense: **it guards the entrance to a broken subsystem instead of deleting it**, and in doing so leaves that subsystem write-only and unreachable while its rationale comment now contradicts the guard. One of the three guard sites is load-bearing; the other two duplicate refusals the shared dispatcher already performs. Recommendation: land it, then do the subtraction as an immediate follow-up (not a someday-maybe) — the guard has already made that subtraction safe.

## Q1 — Is "nested agent fires our hooks" general? Should the guard be shared?

**Exposure is general; the harm is Pi-exclusive, and not because of nesting.** Definitive answer: **do not hoist this guard into `executeAgentHook` or `DispatchLifecycleEvent`.**

Every agent's hook config is installed project-local (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.gemini/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.factory/settings.json`, `.github/hooks/entire.json`, `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`, `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts`) — zero user-global writes. So any agent CLI that reads project config in `-p` mode auto-discovers Entire's hooks when nested. But:

- **Pi is the only agent that resolves session identity out-of-band.** Every other agent takes it from the payload: `claudecode/lifecycle.go:126`, `codex/lifecycle.go:95`, `cursor/lifecycle.go:89`, `geminicli/lifecycle.go:157`, `copilotcli/compat.go:49`, `opencode/lifecycle.go:75`, `factoryaidroid/lifecycle.go:178`. `.entire/tmp/pi/pi-active-session` (`pi/lifecycle.go:287`) is the codebase's only per-repo single-slot identity store.
- **The shared layer already refuses anonymous events, loudly.** `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:168-170` (SessionStart) and `:576-578` (TurnStart) both return `no session_id in %s event`; `:731-733` (TurnEnd) returns `transcript file not specified`. A nested process for any other agent therefore either opens a genuinely separate session (a supported scenario) or is refused.

So the bug was not "nesting reaches our hooks" — it was Pi's cache **manufacturing** identity ahead of a refusal that was already in place. Concretely, of the three new guard sites only one is load-bearing:

| Site | Effect |
|---|---|
| `pi/lifecycle.go:195-200` (session_start) | Redundant with `lifecycle.go:168-170`; only converts a loud error into a silent skip |
| `pi/lifecycle.go:209-212` (before_agent_start) | **Load-bearing** — solely to defuse the cache read three lines below at `:216` |
| `pi/lifecycle.go:233-236` (agent_end) | Defence-in-depth; `:733` would have refused anyway, after logging against the parent session |

A shared `SessionID == ""` skip would be redundant with two existing refusals **and would downgrade them from errors to silent skips across all nine agents** — deleting the exact diagnostic that makes this bug class findable. That is the wrong trade.

**Should it be one mechanism with `shouldSkipForwardedHook`? No — but it should be one mechanism with Copilot's guard.** There are now four sites answering "is this event ours", and they split into two distinct questions:

- *Which agent owns this session*: `hook_guard.go:25` (`shouldSkipForwardedHook`, transcript-path ownership) and `lifecycle.go:86-97` (session-state `AgentType`). Already two layers for one question.
- *Is this the user's top-level session or a subordinate one*: `copilotcli/lifecycle.go:84-96` (skips lifecycle hooks when `sessionId` starts with `toolu_`, because Copilot reuses the Task tool-use id — with a comment describing exactly the same phantom-session harm) and now `pi/lifecycle.go:166`.

The deeper shape is a **declared scope on `agent.Event`** (top-level vs subordinate) that each `ParseHookEvent` sets and the dispatcher enforces once — replacing two prefix/absence heuristics with one field. ---

**It is a trap.** Three concrete costs.

The early return discards it at the source, and adding that feature would require unwinding this design.

---

**Finding — `pi/lifecycle.go:166-168`: the predicate is a one-factor test wearing a two-factor shape, and the extra factor exists to justify a path that cannot occur.** `nestedInvocation` is `sessionID == "" && payload.SessionFile == ""`, but `sessionID` is derived from `payload.SessionFile` by `extractSessionIDFromPath`, which returns `""` only for the empty path (`:410-413`). **Finding — `pi/lifecycle.go:216` and `:238`: the guard made the cache unreachable but left it installed.** `readCachedSessionID` has exactly two production callers, both immediately after a guard that returns whenever `sessionID == ""`; both are now dead. The diff itself concedes that recovery was never usable ("`captureTranscript` returns `""` without a session file, so such an event could only ever fail downstream"), i.e. the subsystem was already vestigial before this change.

Nesting is just the most reproducible instance. The guard fixes the instance; deletion fixes the class.

The honest concept is **"this invocation has no durable session → untracked"**, surfaced once at `session_start` through that existing channel, with `nested` (from the payload) as a separate, silent reason. Naming the predicate after one of its two causes is what will mislead the next reader — the code tests sessionlessness and the docstring already half-admits it ("sessionless (nested)").

---

1. Delete Pi's session-ID cache (`pi/lifecycle.go:216`, `:238` reads; `:201`, `:218`, `:270`, `:287`, `:279-285`), collapse `nestedInvocation` to nothing or to an explicitly-named `untrackedSession(sessionID)`, and drop `TestParseHookEvent_CacheFallbackStillAppliesWithSessionFile`. Pure subtraction; the guard already made it safe.
2. Move the nested signal into the payload (`"nested": true` in `entire_extension.ts:96-137`), keep the extension's handlers registered so the `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` hardening at `:86-93` still applies, and retire `ENTIRE_PI_NESTED` — or, if it must stay, register it in `cmd/entire/cli/provenance` and strip it on spawn per `investigate/env.go:46-59` rather than relying on a "do not read" comment.
3. Unify Pi's and Copilot's subordinate-session suppression (`copilotcli/lifecycle.go:84-96`) behind a declared scope field on `agent.Event`, enforced once in the dispatcher. Leave `shouldSkipForwardedHook` alone — different question.
4. Move the nesting guidance out of the Pi section of `docs/architecture/agent-guide.md:741-755` into the agent-integration contract as a required question for every new agent: *can your CLI be nested in-project, does your payload carry a per-process session id, and can hook discovery be suppressed in the child (à la `--setting-sources ""`)?* All nine hook configs are project-local, so agent #10 will hit this too.</result>

- **Pi is the only agent that resolves session identity out-of-band.** Every other agent takes it from the payload: `claudecode/lifecycle.go:126`, `codex/lifecycle.go:95`, `cursor/lifecycle.go:89`, `geminicli/lifecycle.go:157`, `copilotcli/compat.go:49`, `opencode/lifecycle.go:75`, `factoryaidroid/lifecycle.go:178`. `.entire/tmp/pi/pi-active-session` (`pi/lifecycle.go:287`) is the codebase's only per-repo single-slot identity store.

- **The shared layer already refuses anonymous events, loudly.** `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:168-170` (SessionStart) and `:576-578` (TurnStart) both return `no session_id in %s event`; `:731-733` (TurnEnd) returns `transcript file not specified`. A nested process for any other agent therefore either opens a genuinely separate session (a supported scenario) or is refused.

So the bug was not "nesting reaches our hooks" — it was Pi's cache **manufacturing** identity ahead of a refusal that was already in place. Concretely, of the three new guard sites only one is load-bearing:

| Site | Effect |
|---|---|
| `pi/lifecycle.go:195-200` (session_start) | Redundant with `lifecycle.go:168-170`; only converts a loud error into a silent skip |
| `pi/lifecycle.go:209-212` (before_agent_start) | **Load-bearing** — solely to defuse the cache read three lines below at `:216` |
| `pi/lifecycle.go:233-236` (agent_end) | Defence-in-depth; `:733` would have refused anyway, after logging against the parent session |

A shared `SessionID == ""` skip would be redundant with two existing refusals **and would downgrade them from errors to silent skips across all nine agents** — deleting the exact diagnostic that makes this bug class findable. That is the wrong trade.

**Should it be one mechanism with `shouldSkipForwardedHook`? No — but it should be one mechanism with Copilot's guard.** There are now four sites answering "is this event ours", and they split into two distinct questions:

- *Which agent owns this session*: `hook_guard.go:25` (`shouldSkipForwardedHook`, transcript-path ownership) and `lifecycle.go:86-97` (session-state `AgentType`). Already two layers for one question.
- *Is this the user's top-level session or a subordinate one*: `copilotcli/lifecycle.go:84-96` (skips lifecycle hooks when `sessionId` starts with `toolu_`, because Copilot reuses the Task tool-use id — with a comment describing exactly the same phantom-session harm) and now `pi/lifecycle.go:166`.

The second pair is the real duplication, and it is the second agent-local special case for it. The deeper shape is a **declared scope on `agent.Event`** (top-level vs subordinate) that each `ParseHookEvent` sets and the dispatcher enforces once — replacing two prefix/absence heuristics with one field. Pairing `nestedInvocation` with `shouldSkipForwardedHook` would be the wrong merge.

There is also an existing precedent that outranks detection entirely: `claudecode/generate.go:20-52` passes `--setting-sources ""` so Entire's own spawned `claude` **cannot discover** project hooks. Suppression-at-discovery beats detection-at-parse. Entire can't pass flags to a third-party Pi subagent extension, so it isn't available here — but it is the standard to check for first on every future agent, and worth a line in the agent-integration contract.

---

## Q2 — The env-marker split: trap, and the payload is strictly better

**It is a trap.** Three concrete costs.

**Finding — `entire_extension.ts:23-24`: the marker is information-free at the layer that most invites reading it.** `process.env.ENTIRE_PI_NESTED = "1"` is inherited by every child of the pi process, including the `sh -c "<entire> hooks pi …"` children at `:35-41`. So a hook subprocess sees `"1"` for the legitimate parent *and* for a nested child — the boolean saturates at depth 1 and distinguishes nothing there. The protection is an unenforced comment ("the CLI side must NOT treat it as a skip signal") guarding a variable whose *name* argues the opposite. Maintenance cost: the first person who finds `ENTIRE_PI_NESTED=1` in a hook environment and adds the "obvious" Go-side check silently disables all Pi tracking for every user, and no test in the diff would catch it (`hooks_test.go:46` only asserts the string exists in the installed extension).

**Finding — `entire_extension.ts:23`: it also sits outside the codebase's two established conventions for this exact situation.** (a) `cmd/entire/cli/provenance` is declared the "single source of truth" for hook-visible env names ("These names are stable API"); this is a fifth such marker living in a TypeScript template instead. (b) The canonical treatment for a marker that leaks into nested invocations is *strip on spawn*, not *don't read* — `investigate/env.go:46-59` (`AppendInvestigateEnv`) does exactly this, with a docstring that says "Stripping investigate entries handles nested invocations and stale inheritance from a parent shell." The new marker adopts neither.

**Finding — `entire_extension.ts:23`: the early `return` is a bulk opt-out, not a scoped one.** It returns before any `pi.on` registration, so the nested process loses the *whole* extension — including the `tool_call` handler at `:86-93` that prepends `export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`. A nested `pi --mode json -p` is *more* in need of that hardening than the parent: it is non-interactive by construction while inheriting the parent's TTY, and Entire's git hooks live in `.git/hooks` independently of the extension, so a nested subagent that commits still reaches Entire — now unhardened. This is the classic signature of a special case layered on shared infrastructure: the special case is expressed as "disable everything."

**Declaring nestedness in the payload would be strictly better.** The extension already builds the JSON (`:96-137`) and is the only party that knows its own depth. `"nested": true` is in-band, cannot be inherited, cannot be misread by the wrong process, needs no cross-language convention, and is testable from Go with a JSON fixture. It also survives the case the env marker does not: if Pi's third-party subagent extension spawns the child with an explicit `env:` option, Node **replaces** rather than merges the environment and the marker never arrives — which is precisely why layer 2 exists, and precisely the argument for making layer 2 read a declared fact rather than infer one from absence.

The payload also preserves something the current design destroys permanently: **Pi has no subagent events because the nested process *is* the subagent.** `SubagentStart`/`SubagentEnd` + `SaveTaskStep` already exist and are used by Claude, Cursor, Droid, and Copilot (`lifecycle.go:117-120`, `:1122-1264`). `nested: true` plus the parent session ID in the payload is exactly the data needed to give Pi subagent checkpoints later. The early return discards it at the source, and adding that feature would require unwinding this design.

---

## Q3 — Inferring from absence

**Finding — `pi/lifecycle.go:166-168`: the predicate is a one-factor test wearing a two-factor shape, and the extra factor exists to justify a path that cannot occur.** `nestedInvocation` is `sessionID == "" && payload.SessionFile == ""`, but `sessionID` is derived from `payload.SessionFile` by `extractSessionIDFromPath`, which returns `""` only for the empty path (`:410-413`). The second conjunct can never be false when the first is true — the predicate is exactly `sessionID == ""`. The docstring at `:159-161` justifies the shape by a "legitimate fallback — a session file whose name carries no parseable ID," and `nested_session_test.go:63` enshrines it as `TestParseHookEvent_CacheFallbackStillAppliesWithSessionFile` — while that test's own comment at `:88-89` concedes the cache is not consulted ("the ID comes from the file name itself rather than the cache"). Maintenance cost: the next maintainer reads a two-factor guard plus a test named for a cache fallback, concludes the cache is load-bearing, and does not do the cleanup below.

**Finding — `pi/lifecycle.go:216` and `:238`: the guard made the cache unreachable but left it installed.** `readCachedSessionID` has exactly two production callers, both immediately after a guard that returns whenever `sessionID == ""`; both are now dead. What remains is a **write-only** per-repo file: `cacheSessionID` (`:201`, `:218`), `clearCachedSessionID` (`:270`), `activeSessionFile` (`:287`), the cache half of `resolveSessionDir`, and the seven-line rationale block at `:279-285` that now **contradicts** the guard — it promises recovery when "`agent_end` may fire after Pi has torn down its session manager," which the guard now drops. The diff itself concedes that recovery was never usable ("`captureTranscript` returns `""` without a session file, so such an event could only ever fail downstream"), i.e. the subsystem was already vestigial before this change.

**The deeper alternative is deletion, and it is now a pure subtraction.** Remove the cache read, write, file, and comment; all three guard sites then collapse into the shared layer's existing refusals at `lifecycle.go:168-170`, `:576-578`, `:731-733`. This matters beyond nesting: a single-slot per-repo identity store is unsound for **two concurrent user `pi` sessions in one worktree**, which `CLAUDE.md` explicitly supports ("Supports multiple concurrent sessions — checkpoints from different sessions in the same directory interleave on the same shadow branch"). Nesting is just the most reproducible instance. The guard fixes the instance; deletion fixes the class.

**Finding — `pi/lifecycle.go:166`, `:196-199`: conflating "nested subagent" with "user ran `pi --no-session`" is fine for this fix, not as a permanent shape.** A user's deliberate `pi -p --no-session` in the repo now gets zero tracking behind a `logging.Debug` line (`:170-173`) — invisible by default, with no explanation for missing checkpoints. Entire already has a first-class channel for "capture is off, here's why": `writeUnsupportedPolicySessionStartWarning` / `agentCheckpointCaptureDisabledMessage` (`hook_registry.go:330-358`), which routes through the agent's `HookResponseWriter`. The honest concept is **"this invocation has no durable session → untracked"**, surfaced once at `session_start` through that existing channel, with `nested` (from the payload) as a separate, silent reason. Naming the predicate after one of its two causes is what will mislead the next reader — the code tests sessionlessness and the docstring already half-admits it ("sessionless (nested)").

content.text: The `tool_call` hardening now survives nesting while only lifecycle forwarding is suppressed. Updating the doc to match (it's the canonical home, so it carries the detail):

input.old_string:
- **Nested Pi processes are skipped.** Pi has no subagent events; subagents come from
  an extension (Pi's `subagent/` example) that spawns `pi --mode json -p --no-session`
  with cwd inside the project — where Pi auto-discovers this same extension, so the
  child forwards its own lifecycle too. Two guards: the extension returns early when
  `process.env.ENTIRE_PI_NESTED` is already set (and sets it otherwise, so any Pi it
  spawns is marked), and on the CLI side `nestedInvocation` refuses to resolve a
  payload with no session file against the per-repo session-ID cache. Without the
  latter, a sessionless child was handed its *parent's* session ID and overwrote the
  parent's prompt and turn window with the subagent's internal task text. The env
  marker is read **only** by the extension — Entire's own hook subprocesses inherit
  it, so the CLI must never treat it as a skip signal.
input.new_string:
- **Nested Pi processes do not forward session lifecycle.** Pi has no subagent
  events; subagents come from an extension (Pi's `subagent/` example) that spawns
  `pi --mode json -p --no-session` with cwd inside the project — where Pi
  auto-discovers this same extension, so the child would otherwise forward its own
  lifecycle as the user's session. Two independent guards:

  1. **Extension**: sets `ENTIRE_PI_NESTED` on its process (inherited by any Pi it
     spawns) and, when it is already set, registers only the `tool_call` bash
     hardening and skips the lifecycle handlers. The hardening stays on purpose — a
     nested Pi is non-interactive while inheriting the parent's TTY, and Entire's git
     hooks fire from `.git/hooks` regardless of this extension. The marker is read
     **only** here: Entire's own hook subprocesses inherit it from the parent, so
     treating it as a skip signal in Go would disable tracking for everyone.
  2. **CLI**: `ParseHookEvent` skips any hook whose payload carries no resolvable
     session ID, rather than resolving it against the per-repo session-ID cache —
     that single-slot cache is what handed a sessionless child its *parent's* ID,
     letting the nested turn overwrite the parent's prompt and turn window.
     `session_shutdown` is exempt (it carries no session identity at all and must
     still clear the cache). Same shape as Copilot CLI's subordinate-session guard.

  The guard removed the cache's only two readers, so it is now write-only; removing
  it outright is a follow-up, tracked with the separate problem that a single-slot
  per-repo store cannot represent two concurrent Pi sessions in one worktree.

input.command:
cd /Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2
gh pr edit 1936 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Pi has no subagent lifecycle events. Subagents come from an extension — see Pi's `subagent/` example — which spawns one nested process per task:

```
pi --mode json -p --no-session      # cwd = the project directory
```

Pi auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/*/index.ts` from that cwd, so **the child loads Entire's own extension** and forwards its lifecycle as if it were the user's session. Running `--no-session` it carries no session identity — and the session-ID cache is a single per-repo slot, so resolving against it handed the child its **parent's** ID.

Probed against the real hook entrypoints:

| Child hook | Before |
| --- | --- |
| `session_start` | errors `no session_id in SessionStart event` |
| `before_agent_start` | **succeeds** — overwrites the parent's `last_prompt` with the subagent's internal `Task: …` text and opens a new `turn_id` mid-flight |
| `agent_end` | fails `transcript file not specified` |

So the checkpoint's title and its turn-scoped transcript/token windows described the subagent instead of the user's request.

## Fix

Two independent guards, so neither has to be perfect:

1. **Extension** — sets `ENTIRE_PI_NESTED` on its process (inherited by any Pi it spawns); when already set, it registers **only** the `tool_call` bash hardening and skips the lifecycle handlers. The hardening stays deliberately: a nested Pi is non-interactive while inheriting the parent's TTY, and Entire's git hooks fire from `.git/hooks` regardless of this extension. The marker is read **only** by the extension — Entire's own hook subprocesses inherit it from the parent, so treating it as a skip signal in Go would disable tracking for everyone.
2. **CLI** — `ParseHookEvent` skips any hook whose payload has no resolvable session ID instead of resolving it against the cache. One hoisted guard before the switch, with `session_shutdown` exempt (it carries no session identity at all and must still clear the cache). This is the same shape as Copilot CLI's existing subordinate-session guard, and it also covers third-party subagent extensions and Pi builds that predate the marker.

### Correction to an earlier version of this description

An earlier revision claimed the guard "keeps the legitimate cache fallback — a session file present, but its name carries no parseable ID". **That was wrong**, and it was the only justification offered for an extra term in the predicate. `extractSessionIDFromPath` falls back to the basename, so any real path yields a non-empty ID (`/tmp/live.jsonl` → `"live"`) and that case never reaches the cache. The single input where the two spellings differ is a degenerate basename like `/tmp/x_.jsonl`, which yields `""` *with* a session file present — and there the two-term predicate reported "not nested" and fell through to the cache, i.e. into exactly the leak being fixed. The predicate is now just `sessionID == ""`, which is strictly safer.

### What the guard made dead

Both cache fallbacks are now unreachable and removed. The cache's rationale comment promised recovery when "`agent_end` may fire after Pi has torn down its session manager", which the guard drops — and that recovery never worked anyway: no session file means no transcript, so `captureTranscript` returns `""` and the event died downstream regardless of the ID.

The cache is therefore **write-only** now (written at `session_start`/`before_agent_start`, cleared at `session_shutdown`, read only by tests). The code comment and `agent-guide.md` say so. Removing it outright is left as a **follow-up**, together with the separate problem that a single-slot per-repo identity store cannot represent two concurrent Pi sessions in one worktree — which CLAUDE.md explicitly supports. Nesting was just its most reproducible failure.

## Tests

- `TestParseHookEvent_SessionlessPayloadIsSkipped` — one table in `lifecycle_test.go` (where the package keeps its `ParseHookEvent` coverage): the three sessionless hooks emit no event and leave the cached session untouched; a degenerate `session_file` basename is also skipped; an explicit `session_id` with no session file is still honoured. **Verified RED** against `main`: `emitted TurnStart for session "parent-id"`.
- The pre-existing `TestParseHookEvent_SessionShutdown_ClearsCache` covers the exemption.
- `TestInstallHooks` asserts the installed extension carries the guard.

Also verified end to end against the real binary: after the nested lifecycle, the parent session's `last_prompt` and `turn_id` are unchanged and no second session appears.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" && echo "PR 1936 body corrected"

1	# Agent Implementation Guide
2	
3	Before implementing, read the [Agent Integration Checklist](agent-integration-checklist.md) for design principles (full transcript storage, native format preservation) and validation criteria.
4	
5	## Architecture Overview
6	
7	The Entire CLI uses **inversion of control** for agent integration: agents are passive data providers that translate their native hook payloads into normalized lifecycle events, and the framework handles all orchestration (state transitions, file detection, checkpoint saving, metadata generation). The flow is:
8	
9	```
10	Agent hook invocation → ParseHookEvent() → Event → DispatchLifecycleEvent() → framework actions
11	```
12	
13	An agent never calls strategy methods or manages session state directly. It only answers questions: "What event just happened?" and "What does the transcript say?"
14	
15	## Quick Reference
16	
17	### Core Interface (`Agent`)
18	
19	Every agent must implement all 19 methods on the `Agent` interface:
20	
21	| Group | Method | Purpose |
22	|-------|--------|---------|
23	| **Identity** | `Name()` | Registry key (e.g., `"claude-code"`) |
24	| | `Type()` | Display name for metadata (e.g., `"Claude Code"`) |
25	| | `Description()` | Human-readable description for UI |
26	| | `DetectPresence()` | Check if agent is configured in the repo |
27	| | `ProtectedDirs()` | Directories to preserve during rewind |
28	| **Event Mapping** | `HookNames()` | Hook verbs that become CLI subcommands |
29	| | `ParseHookEvent()` | **Core contribution surface** - translate native hooks to Events |
30	| **Transcript** | `ReadTranscript()` | Read raw transcript bytes |
31	| | `ChunkTranscript()` | Split large transcripts at format-aware boundaries |
32	| | `ReassembleTranscript()` | Recombine chunks into a single transcript |
33	| **Session Management** | `GetHookConfigPath()` | Path to hook config file |
34	| | `SupportsHooks()` | Whether agent supports lifecycle hooks |
35	| | `ParseHookInput()` | Parse hook callback input from stdin |
36	| | `GetSessionID()` | Extract session ID from hook input |
37	| | `GetSessionDir()` | Where agent stores session data |
38	| | `ResolveSessionFile()` | Path to session transcript file |
39	| | `ReadSession()` | Read session data from agent's storage |
40	| | `WriteSession()` | Write session data for resumption |
41	| | `FormatResumeCommand()` | Command to resume a session |
42	
43	### Optional Interfaces
44	
45	| Interface | Methods | When to implement |
46	|-----------|---------|-------------------|
47	| `HookSupport` | `InstallHooks`, `UninstallHooks`, `AreHooksInstalled`, `GetSupportedHooks` | Agent uses a config file for hook registration (e.g., `settings.json`) |
48	| `HookHandler` | `GetHookNames` | **Required for CLI hook registration** — `entire hooks <agent> <verb>` subcommands are only created for agents implementing this interface. Typically delegates to `HookNames()`. |
49	| `TranscriptAnalyzer` | `GetTranscriptPosition`, `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` | You want richer checkpoints with transcript-derived file lists |
50	| `TranscriptPreparer` | `PrepareTranscript` | Agent writes transcripts asynchronously and needs a flush/sync step |
51	| `TokenCalculator` | `CalculateTokenUsage` | Agent's transcript contains token usage data |
52	| `SubagentAwareExtractor` | `ExtractAllModifiedFiles`, `CalculateTotalTokenUsage` | Agent spawns subagents (like Claude Code's Task tool) |
53	| `HookResponseWriter` | `WriteHookResponse` | Agent can display messages from hook responses (e.g., session start banner). Claude Code uses JSON `systemMessage` on stdout; Factory AI Droid uses plain text on stdout. |
54	| `ContextInjector` | `InjectionEvent`, `RenderContextInjection` | Agent can inject text into the **model's** context window (distinct from `HookResponseWriter`, which targets the *user*). The agent declares which lifecycle event it injects at and renders a native stdout payload. The dispatcher (`emitContextInjection`) emits it once per normal session via `session.State.ContextInjectionDecided`, skipping review/investigate sessions, and only when fresh clone-local preferences say trails are enabled for the current repo/API/auth target. The API check happens before the prompt path (`entire enable`, successful `entire trail ...` commands, and stale/missing cache refresh on SessionStart all refresh `ClonePreferences.TrailsEnabled` using `api.Client.TrailsEnabled`); TurnStart performs no auth/network work and leaves unknown/stale caches undecided so a later refresh can still inject. Claude Code / Codex / Gemini inject at `TurnStart` using `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` (UserPromptSubmit / BeforeAgent); Pi and OpenCode emit a `{"inject_context":...}` envelope that their embedded extension applies (Pi via a `before_agent_start` message, OpenCode via `experimental.chat.system.transform`). |
55	| `FileWatcher` | `GetWatchPaths`, `OnFileChange` | Agent doesn't support hooks; uses file-based detection instead |
56

59	### Step 1: Create Package

content.text:
#1936's simplify pass is pushed, with its PR body and trail corrected. #1938's reviews are running.

**#1936 — the reviews found my fix was resting on a false claim.** My predicate was `sessionID == "" && payload.SessionFile == ""`, justified by "keeps the legitimate fallback: session file present, name unparseable." I verified directly: `extractSessionIDFromPath` falls back to the basename, so `/tmp/live.jsonl` → `"live"` — that case never reaches the cache. Two of the four reviewers actually contradicted each other here, so I resolved it by running the function: the *only* input where the two spellings differ is a degenerate basename like `/tmp/x_.jsonl`, which yields `""` **with** a session file present — and there my two-term predicate reported "not nested" and fell through to the cache, i.e. straight into the leak it exists to prevent. Collapsed to `sessionID == ""`, which is strictly safer.

Also applied:

- **Restructured to match the existing precedent I'd missed** — Copilot CLI already solves this exact problem with one hoisted guard plus a negative exemption. Mine was three in-branch copies with three differently-worded `nolint`s. The exemption matters: `session_shutdown` carries no session identity at all, so a blanket guard would have skipped cache cleanup and broken its existing test.
- **Removed the dead cache fallbacks** the guard made unreachable, and corrected the cache's doc comment, which promised a recovery the guard now drops — and which never worked anyway.
- **Fixed a regression I'd introduced**: my early `return` in the extension disabled the `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` bash hardening for nested processes, which need it *more* than the parent (non-interactive but inheriting its TTY, and git hooks fire from `.git/hooks` regardless). Now only the lifecycle handlers are skipped; `tool_call` stays registered.
- Folded three tests into one table in `lifecycle_test.go` where the package keeps `ParseHookEvent` coverage, and dropped a test whose name claimed cache-fallback coverage its own comment admitted it didn't have.

The efficiency review also measured the win: **~351ms and 4 hook subprocesses saved per delegated subagent task**, ~76% of which only the extension guard can recover.

Deferred with a note in the code, the doc, and the PR: the cache is now **write-only** (nothing reads it). Removing it belongs with the separate problem that a single-slot per-repo store can't represent two concurrent Pi sessions in one worktree — which CLAUDE.md explicitly supports.

| call | time | bytes | allocs |

Recursion depth: real data is depth 1 (`transcript.go:429` builds a flat `subagentUsage` with no nesting), so per-call cost is trivial:

| variant | time | bytes | allocs |
|---|---|---|---|
| pre-diff (scalars only) | 172 ns | 48 B | 1 |
| post-diff, with subagents | 209 ns | 96 B | 2 |
| post-diff, no subagents | 70 ns | 48 B | 1 |

The chain depth is therefore attacker/corruption-influenced. It is *not* a stack-overflow risk: `encoding/json` caps nesting at 10000 (measured — depth 9999 decodes, depth 10001 fails with `exceeded max depth`), and 10k tiny frames is nothing against Go's growable stack. Pre-diff this was impossible because the nested total was dropped.

`agent.TokenUsage` is a type alias of `types.TokenUsage` (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/types.go:53`), and `types.AddTokenUsage` (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/types/token_usage.go:23-47`) already does exactly what the post-diff `aggregateTokenUsage` does: nil-if-both-nil, sum the five scalars, recurse into `SubagentTokens`, no mutation. Same semantics, strictly fewer branches, one implementation to keep the depth story consistent with (see finding 2), and it removes a `dupl`-shaped near-clone pair.

### 4. Call frequency — the new recursion is unmeasurable where it runs

`aggregateTokenUsage` is called from exactly one non-test site: `reaggregateFromEntries` (`persistent.go:959`), **once per session** in a `for i := range sessionCount` loop, and `reaggregateFromEntries` itself runs **once per checkpoint write** from `writeCheckpointSummary` (`:801`, reached via `writeStandardCheckpointEntries:686`). Not per blob. `sessionCount` is 1–3 in practice. Each loop iteration already pays `readMetadataFromBlob` — a go-git object lookup + zlib inflate + `json.Decode` of a multi-KB blob, tens of microseconds — so the added ~37 ns / 48 B is well under 0.1% of one iteration. No measurable change.

### 5. `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:312` / `:798` — `withCheckpointSubagentTokens` is as cheap as it can be

One call site, straight-line inside `CondenseSession`, not in a loop; `CondenseSession` runs once per condensing session per commit. Both guard clauses return the input pointer untouched with zero allocation, so the no-subagent case (the common one) costs two nil checks. The fill path does one 48-byte struct copy and **aliases** `checkpointUsage.SubagentTokens` rather than deep-copying it, so there is no second allocation for the nested value. No repeated work, no recomputation, nothing re-read. Nothing to improve here.

### 6. Tests — proportionate, nothing gratuitous

- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/condensation_subagent_tokens_test.go`: 0.18 s + 0.20 s = **0.38 s added to a 40.4 s package (~0.9%)**. Both tests use the shared `setupGitRepo` helper (`phase_wiring_test.go:178`) rather than rolling their own init, and neither repeats setup within a test. They can't be `t.Parallel()` because of `t.Chdir`, so that 0.38 s is wall-clock — acceptable at 0.9%. The real git work is load-bearing: the bug was that the committed root `metadata.json` blob said `null`, so the assertion has to read the blob off the metadata branch (`readCheckpointSummary`); a lighter fixture couldn't prove it. The second test's extra `SaveStep` + `CondenseSessionByID` + second `CondenseSession` is the minimum needed to reach a second checkpoint window with a snapshotted baseline.
- `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/aggregate_token_usage_test.go`: pure function, 5 parallel subtests, no I/O — microseconds. Free.

### Net

Hot-path effect: **strictly better** (avoids ~80 ms per condensing session per commit, at the cost of ~48 bytes). The two changes I'd make are non-hot-path: add the `reviewTokenMaxDepth`-style depth cap to bound the new blob amplification, and collapse `aggregateTokenUsage`/`subagentTokensOf` into the existing `types.AddTokenUsage`.</result>

refactor(checkpoint): use the existing token-summing primitive, and cap its depth

Review of the previous commit found the store-side half was reinventing
types.AddTokenUsage, which already sums the five scalars and recurses into
SubagentTokens, is already imported by persistent.go, and is already used in
production by agentimport. Two reviewers verified equivalence independently, one
by probing both against 7 shapes. Shipping as written would have taken the repo
from three hand-rolled TokenUsage adders to four, with the newest one being the
one whose own comment explained that a field-by-field copy is how the nested
total came to be dropped. aggregateTokenUsage, subagentTokensOf and their new
test are gone; the single caller now calls types.AddTokenUsage.

Propagating the nested total into the root summary turned out to introduce a
write-amplification vector, which the drop had been masking: token usage is read
back from per-session metadata.json blobs on the shared checkpoint branch, so the
chain depth is not trustworthy, and the root summary is re-marshalled with
indentation — O(depth²) in output size. A ~10k-deep chain (json's own nesting
limit) in a 200KB session blob measured out to a ~700MB root blob, written and
pushed. AddTokenUsage now truncates at MaxSubagentDepth = 16, matching the
existing reviewTokenMaxDepth convention. Real chains are depth 1.

Condensation side:

- The fill is now the else-branch of the whole-value fallback above it rather
  than a third sequential assignment. The two are mutually exclusive:
  accumulateTokenUsage already carries SubagentTokens, so the fill's guard always
  early-returned when that branch fired — it was dead work.
- Renamed to withSubagentTokensFrom and used for the identical copy-fill block
  inside applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage (9 lines to 1). The abstraction was
  built and then not applied to the existing caller, leaving the load-bearing
  copy-not-mutate invariant documented in two places that could drift.
- Guards collapsed to one condition; doc comment cut from 26 lines to 15 by
  dropping bug history and a paragraph duplicated at the recompute site.

The live-path comment claimed subagentsDir="" for "the same reason" as the
shadow path. That was inverted: mid-turn the subagent transcripts are still on
disk, so the cleanup hazard cannot apply there — it is the one place the
documented gap could actually be closed. Both comments now say what is true, and
carry the measured ~29x cost that justifies the choice on both paths.

Tests: the new condensation tests folded into the file that already owns subagent
token invariants (renamed subagent_token_dedup_test.go -> subagent_tokens_test.go);
the second one was ~50 lines of arrangement duplicated from the existing
real-reset-path test wrapped around 6 unique assertions, so those assertions now
extend that test instead. The hand-rolled metadata-branch walker is replaced by
the store's own Read, which does not hard-code the sharded layout. A reviewer
disproved the copy-semantics assertions empirically — they pass against a
mutate-in-place implementation, because applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage already
returns a copy on that path — so they are replaced by a direct unit test on the
pure function.
